# Churn Signal Detection

`customer_support.voice_of_customer.churn_signal_detection` · v1.0.0 · **draft**

**Which of these accounts has already started leaving, and what tells us that before they say so?**


> Reading a support relationship for evidence that the customer has begun leaving, early enough that someone can still do something about it. The discipline is almost entirely about resisting the obvious read: the angry ticket feels like the risk and is usually the opposite, because a customer who still argues with us still expects the argument to be worth having. The account that quietly stopped asking has moved its effort somewhere else — often into a migration plan — and it generates no event at all, which is why detection here is a problem of noticing absence against a baseline rather than of catching a signal. Support's output is not a score; it is a briefing that names what changed, whose confidence was lost, and who outside support now owns the conversation.

## Expertise applied


## Outcomes

- Named accounts carry an explicit read of churn risk that states the direction of travel and what changed, not merely that risk is elevated.
- Every raised flag is attributed to a specific behaviour or event, so the account team can act on the cause rather than argue with the score.
- A named owner outside support holds the save conversation, and support's evidence reached them before the renewal window opened rather than during it.
- Accounts that have gone quiet are examined rather than counted as healthy.
- Effort is captured on strategic accounts even where no survey was ever answered.
- Absence of risk on a watched account is recorded as a finding, so that a silent account is distinguishable from an unexamined one.
- Where support cannot see the deciding evidence at all — usage, billing, the competitive conversation — that blindness is stated rather than papered over with tone.


## Failure modes

- Reading anger as the risk. The loudest account is usually the one still trying; the account that stopped writing has already had the internal conversation about replacing us.
- Waiting for the survey. A detractor response arrives after the ticket that caused it, which arrived after the decision it merely confirmed. Anything that depends on the customer choosing to tell us is by construction late.
- Judging contact volume against the queue instead of against the account's own history. A heavy integrator raising fewer tickets and a light user raising more look identical in aggregate and mean opposite things.
- Raising a flag with no receiving owner. A churn risk routed to a dashboard is a note; the account still leaves, and the note is later used as evidence that the system worked.
- Scoring the logo rather than the relationship. Renewals are defended by a person whose credibility was spent on us; when that person changes, the account's history resets even though the score does not.
- Escalating every flag to an executive, which trains the executive to stop reading flags and destroys the channel the genuine cases needed.
- Treating the closed ticket as the end of the exposure. Resolution closes the work item; the effort the customer spent getting there is what they will recall when asked to defend the spend.
- Detecting risk during a live incident, when everyone is angry and the signal has no power to discriminate between accounts.
- Letting support own both the sensing and the intervention. Support can see it and usually cannot fix it — the save is commercial and needs someone able to change terms.
- Suppressing a flag because it cannot be proven. The standard of proof that satisfies a reviewer becomes available after the renewal decision has been taken.
- Confusing an account that no longer needs us with one that no longer wants us. Both go quiet; only one is a loss, and telling them apart needs usage, which support frequently cannot see.


## KPIs

| KPI | Unit | Direction | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| churn_risk_lead_time | days | higher_is_better | How far ahead of the churn or renewal decision the risk was first raised. The only metric here that tests whether the capability is early enough to matter; everything else can look healthy while this one says the flags arrive after the decision.  |
| support_first_detection_share | percent | higher_is_better | Share of churned accounts where support had raised a flag before any other function. Measures whether the earliest sensor is being read, and falls when the briefing cadence lapses long before it falls for any reason to do with detection quality.  |
| flagged_account_save_rate | percent | higher_is_better | Share of flagged accounts retained. Attribution is contested and should be treated as directional. |
| false_positive_rate | percent | target_band | Deliberately a band and not a minimum. Near-zero means the bar has been set where only the undeniable qualifies, and the quiet accounts are being missed; a high rate means the account team has stopped reading flags, which is the same failure by a different route.  |
| quiet_account_review_coverage | percent | higher_is_better | Share of accounts whose contact rate dropped below their own norm that a human actually reviewed. |
| effort_coverage_on_strategic_accounts | percent | higher_is_better | Share of strategic accounts with a current effort read, whether surveyed or reconstructed from ticket history. |
| survey_response_skew | ratio | target_band | How far the responding population diverges from the contacting population. A satisfaction programme answered only by the delighted and the furious is not a measurement, and this is the metric that says so out loud.  |
| flag_to_owner_latency | hours | lower_is_better | Time from a risk being visible in support to it being in the hands of a named owner who can act commercially. |

## Metadata

owner **Customer Support** · updated 2026-08-08 · review **unreviewed** · confidence **provisional**


> Almost nothing in this capability can fire today and the file says so rather than pretending otherwise. Detecting a contact-volume drop needs a per-account baseline the pipeline does not keep; reading effort needs ticket history; reading a relationship change needs a stable requester identity across threads. The nearest thing the substrate genuinely emits is champion_quiet, and binding churn to it would produce a detector that only ever fires on email silence from a single named contact — which is a fragment of the real signal presented as the whole of it. The concrete asks are derived.contact_frequency, contact_rate_per_account and churn_risk_from_support; until those exist this capability is a reading discipline for a human, not an automated detector. What is deliberately absent: any threshold for what counts as a volume drop, any weighting between the triangulation channels, and any risk score. All three are Layer 4's arithmetic, and this file would be wrong to guess at them.
